containers._note: AppJail for the containers module on FreeBSD. Package names and services come from freedomnas-profiles' packages/containers.json; this file holds only what the module runs itself, and how their output reads (*_output, see the module's records.py). Jails, releases, networks and logs live in AppJail's root /usr/local/appjail, OCI images in buildah's /var/db/containers; each is mounted from <pool>/containers/<name> (canmount=on), outside the root dataset, so neither grows the system nor goes back with its rollback. config_files point AppJail's ZFS root at the same dataset (appjail.conf) and buildah's zfs driver at the oci one (storage.conf: without it every image layer becomes a dataset under the root), and keep AppJail's NAT and expose anchors in a block of /etc/pf.conf between # freedomnas appjail begin/end (the rest of the file is left as it is; pass all only when the file has no pass rule of its own); configure enables forwarding and pf, loads the rules, adds the jails' network fnasjails and brings up its bridge with the gateway 10.231.0.1 the way AppJail's network plug does (AppJail itself does it only when the first jail joins, and dnsmasq needs the address to start), and fetches the release; jails find each other by name (appjail-dns writes their names, dnsmasq answers on the network's gateway 10.231.0.1, every new jail gets a resolv.conf naming it; a jail is <name>.fnasjails.appjail); all of it at setup and at every boot (facts: the interface of the default route, the release, the architecture). boot_services enable: the NAT of the jails' network comes from appjail-natnet, and the pool is imported and mounted before services start; running means pf is enabled, AppJail has no daemon. Containers are jails on fnasjails behind NAT: ps lists them tab-separated; logs reads the newest log of the jail's process, else of its console; run reads its words NUL-separated on stdin (xargs -0), because AppJail's options hold spaces (fstab=src dst). Apps are AppJail Director projects named like the app: app_file appjail-director.yml on the app's dataset, its .env beside it (-e), paths in it relative to the file, and the commands run from the app's folder (relative paths such as a template.conf); app_files: the Makejail beside it (Director's default makejail for a service, ./Makejail); compose_check runs Director's own parser on it; update = up --overwrite, remove = down --destroy; up and update turn AppJail's boot flag on for the project's jails and down turns it off (named by describe), because AppJail starts boot jails after FreedomNAS's boot reconcile has run; a project that was never brought up has nothing to stop or describe (check first).

interface.missing: No default route: jails reach the network through the interface of the default route

lines: # Written by FreedomNAS (containers module): AppJail's ZFS root on the pool's dataset.
# Written by FreedomNAS (containers module): image layers on the pool's dataset.
# Written by FreedomNAS (containers module): jails ask the host's dnsmasq, which knows the jails' names.
# Written by FreedomNAS (containers module): DNS for the jails, with their names from appjail-dns.

configure: sh -c 'appjail network list -eHIp name | cut -f1 | grep -qx fnasjails || appjail network add fnasjails 10.231.0.0/24'

sh -c 'ifconfig fnasjails >/dev/null 2>&1 || {{ ifconfig bridge create name fnasjails && ifconfig fnasjails up; }}; ifconfig fnasjails | grep -q "inet 10.231.0.1 " || ifconfig fnasjails inet 10.231.0.1 netmask 255.255.255.0 broadcast 10.231.0.255 description "AppJail network" group appjail_bridge'
containers.ps: appjail jail list -eHIp name status type version ports network_ip4 container_image created
containers.remove_force: sh -c 'appjail stop "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; appjail jail destroy "$1"' remove_force {container}
containers.logs: sh -c 'for t in container console; do f=$(appjail logs list -eHp "jails/$1/$t" 2>/dev/null | sort | tail -n 1); if [ -n "$f" ]; then appjail logs read "jails/$1/$t/$f" | tail -n "$2"; exit; fi; done' logs {container} {lines}
containers.compose_up: sh -c 'cd "${{2%/*}}" && appjail-director -e "${{2%/*}}/.env" up -p "$1" -f "$2" && j=$(appjail-director -e "${{2%/*}}/.env" describe -p "$1" | sed -n "s/^ *\"jail\": \"\(.*\)\",*$/\1/p") && for x in $j; do appjail jail boot on "$x" >/dev/null || exit 1; done' compose_up {project} {file}
containers.compose_update: sh -c 'cd "${{2%/*}}" && appjail-director -e "${{2%/*}}/.env" up --overwrite -p "$1" -f "$2" && j=$(appjail-director -e "${{2%/*}}/.env" describe -p "$1" | sed -n "s/^ *\"jail\": \"\(.*\)\",*$/\1/p") && for x in $j; do appjail jail boot on "$x" >/dev/null || exit 1; done' compose_update {project} {file}
containers.compose_down: sh -c 'appjail-director check -p "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0; cd "${{2%/*}}" && j=$(appjail-director -e "${{2%/*}}/.env" describe -p "$1" | sed -n "s/^ *\"jail\": \"\(.*\)\",*$/\1/p") && appjail-director -e "${{2%/*}}/.env" down -p "$1" && for x in $j; do appjail jail boot off "$x" >/dev/null || exit 1; done' compose_down {project} {file}
containers.compose_remove: sh -c 'appjail-director check -p "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0; cd "${{2%/*}}" && appjail-director -e "${{2%/*}}/.env" down --destroy -p "$1"' compose_remove {project} {file}
containers.app_members: sh -c 'appjail-director check -p "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0; cd "${{2%/*}}" && appjail-director -e "${{2%/*}}/.env" describe -p "$1"' app_members {project} {file}
containers.tls_copy: sh -c 'umask 077 && install -o "$1" -g "$2" -m 600 "$3" "$4" "$5" && cat "$4" "$3" > "$5/.tls.pem" && chown "$1:$2" "$5/.tls.pem" && mv "$5/.tls.pem" "$5/tls.pem" && printf %s "$6" > "$5/hostname" && chown "$1:$2" "$5/hostname"' tls_copy {uid} {gid} {cert} {key} {path} {hostname}

ui.volumes_label: Folders, one per line (/path of the pool : /path in the jail)
ui.run_hint: A jail mounts folders only: a path like /tank/media, then the path in the jail. Ports are host:jail, with /udp for UDP; the jail sits on its own network behind NAT.
ui.app_example:
options:
  - virtualnet: "fnasjails:<random> default"
  - nat:
services:
  web:
    name: site-web
    makejail: ./Makejail
    options:
      - template: /usr/local/share/examples/appjail/templates/freebsd-oci.conf
      - expose: "8080:80"
    volumes:
      - html: /usr/local/www/nginx
volumes:
  html:
    device: ./html
